per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a prefix, not an object. The nearest equivalent is the block size, and the free allocation is one /48, which the page states as Free · 65,536 /64s

retention.notes: Whether a free /48 persists indefinitely is unverified. The page states no duration for it and no order was placed, so the absence of a term is read off a page rather than confirmed by a subscription record.

egress.terms: No traffic term is published for a prefix, because the bytes never cross IPYE: the block is announced from a user's own compute. The only traffic statement on the site belongs to the server bundles: 'Our Datacenter Bundles come natively provisioned with 10 Gbps unmetered upstream ports, ensuring your commercial VPNs never face peak-hour throttling, scaling transparently as active users surge.'
egress.free_allowance: none published; a prefix carries no traffic of its own

interface_detail: Ordering is a web checkout and nothing else: my.ipye.com/products/ipv6-rental/48-ipv6/checkout asks for ASN(s), Region and Intended Use, with name servers for rDNS optional, and returns 200 with an order summary of $0.00. No endpoint for ordering or for prefix management is documented. The vendor states an API for a different job, DNS and geolocation: 'Take absolute control via our API and dashboard' and 'Dashboard API provides programmatic access for bulk Reverse DNS (rDNS/PTR) modifications'. The prefix itself is reached by announcing it over BGP from a user's own routing daemon; that is a network interface, and the schema's token list has no name for it.
tooling: A routing daemon on the client's side: bird or FRR on the host that originates the prefix, plus the LOA the portal generates. No wrapper exists and none is needed; the checkout is a form and the portal is the management surface. rDNS and PTR edits are the one programmatic path, and only after an account exists.
chaining: Take the free /48, announce it from a user's own compute under an origin ASN, and every request leaving that host presents an address in a prefix a user controls; that is one prefix in one network, so it meets a gate counting the /64 and not a gate counting the ASN.

limits_note: Not a vocabulary kind, kept so it is not lost: the $300 one-time IPv6 Registration is a provider-independent allocation under your company at ARIN or RIPE and needs a company; the $500 one-time ASN Registration needs a company registration certificate, proof of ID for the administrative contact and a signed framework agreement. Neither is required to take the free /48 with a rented shared or dedicated ASN.
binding_note: 45 GB a month across about 599,000 requests meets no byte quota and no address cap here, because the prefix carries no traffic of its own; the first thing that stops a user is that the free /48 cannot be announced until an origin ASN exists, and the ASN behind IPYE's shared-ASN product could not be identified from RIPE without placing an order.

identity_cost.detail: An account at my.ipye.com is required to order, and the vendor says the account costs no identity document: the homepage carries 'No KYC/ID Verification Required', the /asn page description reads 'Crypto accepted, no KYC required', and the free /48 checkout asks for ASN(s), Region and Intended Use rather than a document. The exception is a different product on the same site: ASN Registration at $500 one-time requires a Company Registration Certificate (LLC, LTD), proof of ID for the administrative contact and a signed framework agreement. A rented shared ($300/yr) or dedicated ($700/yr) ASN is not described as requiring any of that.

reliability_note: One prefix is one network: every /64 in the /48 is announced by the same origin ASN, so a gate counting the ASN or the /48 sees one client however many addresses are used. The vendor states 'We don't shut down your servers for typical bulk operations'; that is a claim, not a measurement. Whether the free /48 is registered to an eyeball ISP as /use-cases describes is unverified, because no block was obtained.
confidence_note: Every price, the ASN requirement and the KYC claim were read from the vendor's own pages on 2026-10-24, and the RIPE check was run but establishes only a negative. Measured would need an ordered /48, the prefix in hand, the prefix's registration confirmed against RIPE, and one refusal captured from an upstream that refuses Cloudflare's ranges.

notes: Three readings of the free /48 were considered. (1) It is a lead magnet that does not exist at the stated price: refuted, because the order page returns 200 with an order summary of $0.00 and three required fields. (2) /pricing 404ing means the offer is unpublished: refuted the same way, and the 404 is recorded as a probe rather than treated as evidence of absence. (3) The free tier is a /48 of IPYE's own datacenter space and the eyeball-ISP sentence on /use-cases is about the paid ISP bundles only: not refuted. The /ipv6-rental page never repeats the registration-class claim for the free /48, and no block was obtained, so the class of the free block is unverified and this record does not claim it. What the record does establish is narrower and firmer. The /48 is $0, it is a real order, it comes with an automatic RPKI ROA and route object, and it is unusable until an origin ASN exists. That last fact is the binding one and it is the vendor's own sentence, not an inference. Size is not diversity: 65,536 /64s are one prefix in one network, so the product meets a gate counting the /64 and leaves a gate counting the ASN untouched unless the prefix is announced from a different ASN than the compute, which is a fact about the announcement and not about the registration. The ASN itself is the open question. A RIPE searchcomplete for IPYE returns no ASN, so the network the shared ASN sits in cannot be named before paying $300/yr, and whether that ASN is a hosting ASN or an eyeball ASN decides whether this product reaches rung 5 at all. Two discrepancies are recorded rather than smoothed. The homepage as read on 2026-10-24 says 'No KYC/ID Verification Required', and the word Number does not appear on it. The interface tokens are a deliberate deviation. The record therefore uses rest for the stated rDNS API and cli for the BGP announcement, and puts the web checkout and the missing name for a network interface in interface_detail. No record in another topic is corrected by this one.
